title: Cleaning up a biohazardous spill in a biosafety cabinet
author: Steven W Wilhelm
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wghfbt6
materials: Segregate contaminated cleanup materials into the appropriate biohazardous waste containers.

steps.title: Maintain BSC airflow
steps.instruction: Leave the biosafety cabinet (BSC) running throughout the cleanup; do not turn it off.

steps.title: Remove broken glass
steps.instruction: Using forceps, tweezers, or other appropriate tools, pick up any broken glass from the spill and place it into a sharps container. Do not wipe the glass.

steps.title: Apply disinfectant to spill
steps.instruction: Pour (do not spray) disinfectant onto the contaminated surface, starting at the periphery of the covered spill and moving inward, ensuring the entire area is covered. Allow the disinfectant to remain for the appropriate contact time.

steps.title: Wipe up spilled material
steps.instruction: After the required contact time has elapsed, wipe up the spilled material.

steps.title: Reapply disinfectant if needed
steps.instruction: Reapply disinfectant to the affected area, allow the appropriate contact time again, then wipe the area. Repeat this cycle until the surface is clean.

steps.title: Remove items post‑disinfection
steps.instruction: Only after the disinfection steps are complete may any items be removed from the cabinet.
